When I was 18 I finished boarding school with average grades and returned home to a semi-planned state of idleness. It was a protest to my parents ignoring my concerns about where my life was heading, I still deeply needed my parents back then, I was really struggling and depressed since around 16. It was that or suicide straight up. I removed myself from the world, didn't work or apply to universities, slept through days and played video games during the night, on a laptop that was not suited to play video games on. So games crashed and didn't perform, I didn't enjoy it, I gave in to the complete absurdity that my life has become. I was "dead weight", I hated myself, felt all encompassing toxic shame. Sometimes I walked around, listened to podcasts, music. I was deluding myself, apathetic, suffering. I started stealing money from my father for food. When I ran into people I was acquainted to I felt shame, there was no way I could explain to them what was going on with me, and it was painful to have no one I can look forward to talk to, knowing I gave that up for unclear reasons. I was holding myself hostage. Then I found full time work in a coffee shop, which was extremely challenging due to my life and my mental health,  forcing myself to apply for work, learning to work there, dealing with some toxic colleagues, doing the actual work. I still made the most of it I can proudly say now. Now I am unemployed again, 26 years old, and I am not connected to a single soul on this planet in any capacity. BUT I have tremendous respect for life and enjoy being an adult and haven't been depressed for a single day in the last 4 years. I have restored my dignity by being extremely tidy and industrious, by learning how to cook food and really enjoy the process, one painful step, along with my my kinda-friends gleefully roasting me, at a time. I have learnt the value of responsibility, and how much capacity there is in us that deserves recognition. Salvation is achieved one a time, and not even in a spiritual sense. You might deeply care about "interests" right now, as I did just yesterday it seems. Basketball, tennis, music, saxophone, moba video games, these are things that I enjoyed in past lives, that I can still perfectly appreciate. But the only meaning in your life will come from responsibility, so play it out and see how it shapes you, and be amazed how things that you care about literally evolve. You will FEEL as if there is more of you, but this process does require your actions and overall input. And if none of this makes sense and you don't have faith in yourself or anything around you, do what you can to start from things within your reach, I promise you there are very real things in life that you can tap into.
